Hi Sarah,
I apologize for this additional issue, but I wanted to confirm my
assessment before contacting you directly. This involves the BC04 rather
than the THOR P2; my BC04 was included in order number ····-A. I mentioned
this to Mike via Discord the gentleman who used to appear in videos with JD
but I noticed that when Helium deploys mails its products, it ships them
only in the box containing the miner, without an outer box for better
transport. My BC04 arrived in its box inside what I believe was an Amazon
bag. I will send photos, but essentially it was opened from the top; at
that time I hadn’t realized there is a seal at the bottom. (In the past
month I have purchased about 14 miners from different companies, so I have
been opening a lot of boxes. But I purchased another BC04 from Altair Tech,
and they ship their miners in their box but then put it in another box for
better transport. Anyway, as you see in the photos, my miner box came a
little more beat up and it was opened from the top.)

My concern is that I was comparing the Altair Tech shipped BC04 fan and the
Helium deploys BC04. If you look at the screenshot, when the Helium deploy
fan is at 100 percent it is only doing 2784 RPM, the chip is at 57.5 and
VRM at 71. But when you see the Altair Tech BC04 fan at 87 percent it is
doing 3517 RPM and is keeping the chip cooler along with the VRM chip at
51.4 and 57.3. You will also hear in the video how the Altair Tech BC04 is
louder and moving more air than the Helium deploy at 100 percent. I had
recently gotten the Altair BC04 so I was not able to compare until now.At
the time, I overlooked how the HD-shipped BC04 opened from the top, whereas
the Altair BC04 was unsealed from the bottom and opened upward. Tampering
might be possible, though I am unsure. Something is clearly wrong with the
fan’s operation. As I mentioned, I have ordered many miners and received a
lot of mail, so I should have paid closer attention to the box; initially
the HD BC04 seemed fine, but comparing them at the same specifications
shows something unusual with the HD unit. Although both use the same
firmware, the overclock settings display different frequency and core
voltage values; to ensure a fair comparison, I manually adjusted the HD
BC04 frequency to match the Altair, since overclock mode does not allow
changes.

Regardless, I recommend that HD ship products in the original miner box
plus an outer box for better protection perhaps that explains the odd noise
from the Thor’s PSU. My BC04 arrived only in the original box inside an
Amazon bag and opened from the top rather than the seal, suggesting
possible interference; the fan still performs poorly when compared directly
with the Altair unit. I apologize for being long-winded, but I would
appreciate assistance because the fan seems odd. Both units share the same
firmware number.

Hi Javier,

I am Hal, the technical side of HeliumDeploy, and Sarah passed your BC04 question to me. Thank you for the detail, an A/B against a second identical unit on the same firmware is exactly the kind of test that makes my job easy, so no apology needed for the length.

First, one practical thing: your videos and photos came through as Google Drive links, and those do not open for me from our side. If you can attach the files directly to a reply in this thread I will look at every one of them. I do not want to tell you what I think a video shows when I have not watched it.

On the numbers you gave me, your reading is right and the fan is the odd part. 2784 RPM at 100 percent against 3517 RPM at 87 percent on the same model and firmware is roughly a quarter short, and the temperature gap follows it exactly: VRM 71 against 57.3, ASIC 57.5 against 51.4. The chip is reporting the PWM duty it is asking for, not what the fan is actually delivering, so a fan with bearing drag, a slightly different fan revision, or a 12V rail sagging under load all look like "100 percent" in the UI while moving less air. Nothing in those readings points to a board problem: all four chips are present and hashing, and there is no VREG or TPS error, which is what a damaged unit normally throws. 71C on the VRM is warm but still inside safe operating range, so you are not doing damage by running it, though I would leave it off overclock until this is settled.

Three checks will tell us which of the three causes it is, and they cost nothing. With the unit unplugged, spin the fan by hand: a good one coasts freely for a second or two, a failing bearing feels gritty or stops dead. Then unseat and reseat the 4-pin fan connector on the board, make sure the intake and the fins are clear, and power it back up. Last, and this is the decisive one since you have two units side by side: swap the 12V bricks between the HD BC04 and the Altair BC04 and watch the RPM at 100 percent. If the RPM follows the brick, the power supply is sagging. If the low RPM stays with the HD unit on a known good brick, the fan itself is weak and the fix is a new fan, not the miner. Send me the result along with the exact firmware build string from both units and the BC04 serial from the label, and I will have the full picture.

On the box: I cannot tell from here whether it was opened before it reached you, and I am not going to guess at that. What I can say is that nothing in your readings looks like swapped or missing hardware, the chip count and behaviour are normal, and the serial will let us confirm the unit against what left the warehouse. I have passed your packaging point and the photos of the box on with the rest of this, because an outer carton is a fair request and worth the team hearing from someone who opens as many of these as you do.

I have written up the fan findings for JD, our hardware lead. The team is offline for the weekend and picks this up Monday at 10am ET, and their answer comes to you right here by email. If you want a faster read in the meantime, JD is very active on our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf as @nullhashrate, and he will know the name (contact hidden).

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Two ways round it. The simplest is to trim each clip down to ten or fifteen seconds in your phone's photo editor, just the part where the fan is running and the reading is visible, and attach the trimmed files straight to a reply here. Short clips usually slip under the attachment limit. The other way, and honestly the better one for video, is to drop them in our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and tag @nullhashrate. With the unit unplugged, spin the fan by hand and tell me whether it coasts freely or feels gritty. Reseat the 4-pin fan connector and check the intake and fins are clear. Then swap the 12V bricks between the two BC04s and watch the RPM at 100 percent: if the low RPM follows the brick, it is the power supply, and if it stays with the HD unit on a known good brick, the fan itself is weak.

Alongside that, a screenshot of the status page of each unit at 100 percent, the exact firmware build string from both, and a photo of the BC04 serial label give me everything I need. Keep it off overclock until we know, 71C on the VRM is safe but there is no reason to push it.

Hi Javier,

The photos came through perfectly this time and they settle it. I can read all three clearly: your BC04 serial label is SN (number hidden), and the two thermal screens show your unit at Fan 1 100 percent (2810 RPM) with Hashboard 1 at 57.8C, VRM 71.8C and HB1 at 4.55V, against the other unit at Fan 1 100 percent (3762 RPM) with Hashboard 1 at 50.8C and VRM 56.5C. Both are running the exact same firmware, 3.0.5 20260909 v1.2.0, both are BM1370, and both report Safe.

That is the whole picture in one frame. Same firmware, same chip, same 100 percent command, and almost 1000 RPM of difference. Since swapping the power supply changed nothing, the brick is out of it, and since the controller is asking for full duty and getting less air, the fan itself is the weak link. The hand-spin test being inconclusive is normal, by the way, a fan can be down 25 percent on airflow and still feel fine between your fingers, so do not worry that you missed something.

What that means practically: there is nothing wrong with the board or the chips on your unit. It is hashing, the hashboard sits at 57.8C and the VRM at 71.8C, both still inside safe operating range even at the worse of the two readings. You are not damaging anything by running it. The fix here is at the fan, not the miner, so please do not open or swap anything yourself.

I have written the full comparison up with the serial, both screens, the firmware build and the PSU swap result and passed it to JD, our hardware lead, since getting a fan out to you is his call and not something I can do from my side. The team is off for the weekend and picks this up Monday at 10am ET, and the answer comes to you right here.

Until then, run it in normal mode rather than overclock, keep it out of a cabinet or anywhere the intake is close to a wall, and it will sit happily where it is. If you want JD's eyes on it sooner, he is on our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf as @nullhashrate and the videos will play fine for him there.

Thanks for running the tests properly, Javier, your data did most of the diagnosis.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Hi guys any idea what might be going on with the fan?

Javier M. (phone hidden)

Hi Javier,

Yes, and the short answer is that the fan on your unit is simply not delivering what the controller is asking of it.

Here is the reasoning in plain terms. The percentage you see in the UI is the duty cycle the controller is commanding, not a measurement of airflow. The R. figure next to it is what the fan's tachometer wire actually reports back. On your unit those two disagree: it is being told 100 percent and only returning 2810 RPM, while the second BC04, same BM1370 chip, same firmware build 3.0.5 20260909 v1.2.0, same command, returns 3762 RPM. That gap of roughly 950 RPM is about 25 percent less rotation, and airflow falls off faster than RPM does, so the heat picture follows exactly as you would expect: VRM 71.8C against 56.5C, hashboard 57.8C against 50.8C.

There are only three realistic causes, and all three sit at the fan rather than the miner. One is a worn or dragging bearing, which is the most common and often silent to the touch, which is why your hand-spin test felt inconclusive. Two is a different fan revision fitted at the factory, a lower static pressure or lower max RPM part that happens to be in that batch. Three is a partly blocked or recirculating intake, though your readings held steady under load, which argues against it. What we have ruled out firmly is the power supply, because swapping the brick changed nothing, and the firmware, because both units run the identical build. Nothing points at the board itself: all chips are present, the unit hashes, and there is no VREG or TPS error anywhere on the screen.

So the fix is a fan, not a miner. That part is with JD, our hardware lead, along with your serial, both screenshots and the test results. The team is off for the weekend and picks it up Monday at 10am ET, and their answer comes to you right here in this thread.

In the meantime you are safe to keep running it in normal mode rather than overclock, with the intake clear of walls and shelving. Both temperatures read Safe even at the worse figures, so nothing is being damaged while this gets sorted. If you want a second pair of eyes sooner, JD is on our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf as @nullhashrate, and your videos will play fine for him there.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support
